objective: Maximize alpha-stage terminal wealth by preserving the two-campaign diversification benefit while allocating simultaneous vacancy capital in proportion to the already-causal opportunity scores instead of mechanically splitting cash 50/50.

root_evidence.lesson: Removing the second campaign slot destroys wealth in all three fixed scopes, so diversification across two independent campaigns is economically valuable. The remaining concentration hypothesis is funding share, not capacity.
root_evidence.current_funding_semantics: The alpha-decay owner selects up to max_positions vacancies by causal score but then divides all observed cash equally among the simultaneously chosen vacancies, regardless of score separation.

treatment.capacity: Keep exactly the current two campaign slots.
treatment.selection: Keep the exact campaign-peak champion candidate ranking, eligibility, tie-break and lifecycle decisions.
treatment.trigger: Only when the unchanged champion decision contains one alpha-decay VACANCY_FILL event on the current close with two or more newly chosen symbols and observed cash > 0.
treatment.allocation: For those simultaneously chosen vacancies only, allocate the same observed cash in direct proportion to their strictly positive current causal scores: cash_j = observed_cash * score_j / sum(chosen_scores). Existing funded units are untouched.
treatment.single_vacancy: If exactly one symbol is chosen, return the exact champion decision byte-for-economic-behavior unchanged.
treatment.state: Do not change pending_alpha_reference, owned_alpha_reference, retirement, invalidation, campaign-peak state, or any eligibility state. The parent has already causally registered those values before the target units are reweighted.
treatment.execution: Convert each chosen cash_j to target economic units using the same current close marks used by the parent decision. Never spend expected sale proceeds; only observation.cash is allocated. Preserve unchanged next-session execution, fees, slippage, ADV/liquidity, limits, T+1 and lot rules.
treatment.no_continuous_rebalance: After inventory is actually funded, do not rebalance held campaign weights because scores change. This family affects admission funding only.

structural_difference.single_dominant_campaign: Retains two slots rather than deleting diversification; concentration varies endogenously with causal score separation only at simultaneous admission.
structural_difference.allocation_auction: Does not solve a two-leg notional/risk polygon or alter an older support owner. It leaves the current offensive lifecycle intact and changes only the equal-cash split of already-selected simultaneous admissions.
structural_difference.opportunity_allocation: Does not change residual funding for later second campaigns or add rank-implied fixed fractions. It only divides the exact same current observed cash among candidates selected on the same close.
structural_difference.breadth_concentration: No breadth regime, no capacity change and no repeated portfolio rebalancing.

measurement.primary: mean(log(terminal wealth)) across the three fixed scopes
measurement.promotion: Treatment must strictly exceed campaign-peak mean-log and must not reduce campaign-peak minimum terminal wealth.
measurement.if_promoted: Immediately evaluate the identical source-bound treatment over all 896 frozen sessions before formal-matrix expansion.

prohibitions: no fixed 60/40, 70/30 or other weight grid
no capacity retry or position-count search
no future labels or reference-strategy source consumption
no post-result edit of this family
